limitations: Reviewed only the serialized JSON, including original packet history and supplied quotations; no tools, external pages, files or remembered target results were used.
Cannot attest that quotations or transcribed facts match external webpages. Market publication dates and several factual details rely on packet metadata or curator assertions.
The 2026-05-15 cutoff was treated as an information-availability boundary, not execution time.
No target financial outputs were supplied, so implementation of the fixed reconciliation adjustment and output arithmetic cannot be certified.

findings.subject: Unsupported portions of material market claims
findings.finding: The original quotations do not establish retention of 85%/86%, personal written-premium contraction excluding Canada, longer recovery times or declining injury frequency, April goods inflation of 2.0%, or larger invested assets as an investment-income growth cause. These details appear in curator factual_datapoint fields, without located factual extracts or fuller original text. Research repeats them and scenario reasoning uses several of them. Their support is transcription-dependent; acknowledging this limitation does not independently verify the claims.

findings.subject: Underlying versus all-in combined ratio
findings.finding: Research states that Q1's '85.3% combined ratio includes expenses as well as losses.' Original history identifies 85.3% as the underlying combined ratio and 88.6% as the combined ratio. This unresolved labeling contradiction matters because catastrophes and reserve development are separately modeled. Finance and scenario use the underlying measure correctly, but the research statement cannot pass unchanged.

findings.subject: Finance mapping and reconciliation
findings.finding: The supplied historical quotations support the material premium baselines, percent-to-decimal conversions, catastrophe sign conversion, quarterly versus year-to-date selection, core tax calculations and earnings bridge. The fixed Q2 2025 residual of -36.913 million is consistent with 1,022-315-(-927)-10,921*(1-0.847). Its decimal precision is arithmetic precision from rounded inputs, not forecast accuracy.

findings.subject: Scenario bounds and counterfactual changes
findings.finding: All nine scenario drivers remain within contract bounds. Every base and bull value matches the frozen control; only bear written growth changes from -5% to -6% and bear underlying ratio from 88% to 89%. These are explicitly illustrative sensitivities, with appropriate adverse profitability orientation. Written growth does not directly affect the contracted earnings equation.

findings.subject: Causal interpretation and double counting
findings.finding: The scenario avoids direct substitution of global pricing, social inflation, drought prevalence or policy rates into company financial drivers. Severity stresses are jointly capped; catastrophes, current-year underwriting and prior-year development remain separate. Historical yield effects and Canadian disposal are not charged again. Zero favorable development is appropriately disclosed as excluding adverse reserve strengthening.

findings.subject: Cash-flow quarter assignments
findings.finding: Supplement quotations contain amounts but omit column headers. They cannot independently establish the stated quarter assignments for 2,198 million and 2,334 million. Finance appropriately treats these as serialized-record context and supplies no cash forecast; these mappings remain unverified.

findings.subject: Information availability
findings.finding: All supplied publication dates precede the cutoff. Q1 2026 disclosures are eligible for the mid-market vintage, and no Q2 2026 realized outcomes appear in the reviewed responses. This checks internal date eligibility only; publication dates were not externally authenticated.
